title: Held camera render-clock alignment and pickup reach: null-guard correction
acceptance_criteria: Canonical carrier view supplies explicit render-parent identity and its existing body-feet offset; snapshot codec retains this relation and unchanged non-carrier view fields.

Held camera translation follows the holder model's xOld/yOld/zOld sample at the same partial tick, cancelling independent body snapshot lead/noise while preserving native eye placement and detached-camera behavior.

Contained presentation uses stable committed identity rather than prediction tracker permission; correction is limited to the exact camera body and matching loaded parent and stops on cleared or missing association.

Client item and portable-living nominations reuse the server's physical pickup reach predicate, including null/non-finite rejection, retain aim tolerance and item priority, and leave block-use reach and server authority unchanged.
Camera mixin transforms successfully in a fresh isolated native client startup. Startup is not held-POV or connected visual acceptance.
Fresh focused JVM, full native and affected interaction/prediction readiness pass before packaging; same-holder escape transfer and remote release/jump presentation remain unresolved.
manual_steps: As a playable mouse, be held by another player. Have the holder walk, sprint, stop/start, turn and jump; check smooth relative motion and no camera lead.
Check the previous camera distance/placement and free look. Repeat while critical if possible, then drop and pick up again; no stale holder offset should remain.
Check disposal-unit view/flush and catching moving mice/jugs near the reach boundary. Targets moving beyond server reach can still be denied.
Hand-transfer escape, remote drop glide and repeated-jump observer landings are not claimed fixed.
